Pressure rose steadily to 3.329 Torr, about +0.05 Torr every 120 s, with no sign of levelling off

O2 exhaust sensor not installed, so the growth atmosphere cannot be verified

args.missing_evidence: Exhaust O2 or another leak check, such as a helium leak test or a pressure rate-of-rise test with the pump isolated, to tell an air leak (seal leak) from a restricted exhaust or pump line (exhaust blockage). Also a check of the exhaust valve and pump.

After EVERY observation event, call report_assessment exactly once with your current judgment:

    SUPPORTING: characterization shows the target outcome.
    NEGATIVE: execution was normal and characterization shows the target was not achieved;
      this is evidence about the recipe.
    INCONCLUSIVE: characterization exists but cannot count as evidence about the recipe
      (for example because execution was anomalous, or the result is ambiguous).
    NOT_YET_AVAILABLE: no characterization of the sample exists yet.
- attribution: if execution is anomalous, which layer: instrument_process, sample_handling,

- missing_evidence: what observation would resolve anything you cannot yet determine.

set = setpoints (T in °C, Ar in sccm); obs = readings: T thermocouple °C, Pheat heater power %,
Ar argon flow sccm, P tube pressure Torr, O2 exhaust oxygen ppm, status = controller status.
When present, ref gives [mean, sd] of each reading at this time across normal runs. A device manifest is sent
with the first event and again whenever it changes. It lists which sensors this furnace has
installed. Telemetry values are null for sensors that are not installed.
Speak at most one short sentence per event, and only if your judgment changed.

content.text:
I've flagged the run as anomalous and recommended calling a person in. Tube pressure was normal when growth started (3.04 Torr at 2520 s, matching the ramp). Since then it has risen steadily to 3.33 Torr at 3240 s, about 0.05 Torr every two minutes, with no sign of levelling off. Over the same stretch, argon flow stayed at about 100 sccm and temperature held at 750 °C with steady heater power. So the rise isn't coming from the gas flow or the heating.

- **Likely causes:** either air is leaking in (a seal leak) or the exhaust line is restricted (an exhaust blockage). Both can raise pressure this way.
- **Why I can't narrow it down:** this furnace has no exhaust O2 sensor. Rising oxygen would point to a leak, and without that reading I also can't confirm the growth atmosphere is clean.
- **What would settle it:** a leak check, such as a helium test or shutting off the pump and watching how fast pressure rises, plus a look at the exhaust valve and pump.

No sample has been characterised yet, so there's no scientific result so far. If a sample is measured after this run, it shouldn't count as a test of the recipe unless the pressure problem is explained.
